How design becomes a real page

The workflow from approved prototype to live site — and where market differences and copy live.

1 Prototype approved
HTML prototype → Next.js page
Once a prototype is signed off, the builder implements it as a real Next.js page at src/app/(site)/[market]/ using the same CSS tokens. The prototype becomes the spec. Both run in parallel until the Next.js version replaces the static one.
2 Sanity CMS setup
Content management at /studio
Sanity Studio at /studio gives you and the team a visual editor for all content — products, SDS files, homepage copy, team bios, partner profiles. No code deploys needed for content changes.
3 AU vs NZ differences
Market field on every document
Each Sanity document (product, homepage, partner) has a markets field. Example: Melfred Borzall reamers tagged markets: [nz] only appear on /nz/products/tooling. AU gets only AU-stocked products. One template, two market outputs.
NZ full tooling range AU subset only
4 Copy per market
Two homepage documents in Sanity
Homepage NZ and Homepage AU are separate Sanity documents — same template, different content. Hero headline, eyebrow, CTA copy, and market-specific callouts all live in Sanity. You edit copy in Studio; it publishes live without a code deploy.
Homepage NZ doc Homepage AU doc
5 SDS files in Sanity
PDFs stored in Sanity, linked everywhere
SDS PDFs are uploaded once to Sanity as file assets on the product document. They auto-appear on the product detail page and in the /sds searchable index. Update a PDF in Sanity and it updates everywhere instantly — no code change required.
6 Build order
What gets built in what order
  • → Sanity schemas + Studio setup
  • → Products connected to Sanity (fluids, tooling, grease)
  • → Homepage NZ + AU from Sanity content
  • → SDS library (product pages + /sds search)
  • → Mud School page
  • → llms.txt, sitemap.xml, robots.txt
